findings.title: Team/org auth SQL is an ungrouped OR, so extra AND filters skip team bookings
findings.body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition return a top-level OR, e.g. (("teamId" = ANY(...)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)) OR (("userId" = ANY(...)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false)), with no parentheses around the whole predicate. getBaseConditions returns that fragment unchanged whenever there is no eventTypeId/memberUserId filter (the common path; date bounds are not part of InsightsBookingServiceFilterOptions and must be applied by the caller). AND binds tighter than OR, so WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" >= ${start} AND "startTime" < ${end} is parsed as (team-booking match) OR (personal-booking match AND date range). Every team booking for that team/org is returned with no time bound, and any other caller AND (event-type allow-list, status, extra auth) is likewise dropped for the team-booking side. The same trap exists on the public event-type filter at the ungrouped OR in buildFilterConditions ("eventTypeId" = $1 OR "eventParentId" = $1): WHERE auth AND that fragment becomes (auth AND eventTypeId = $1) OR eventParentId = $1, which can return rows outside authorization. getBaseConditions only parenthesizes when both auth and filters are present, and the tests assert the ungrouped form, so they do not catch this. Wrap every returned fragment in an outer (...) so it is one grouped predicate before it is embedded.

findings.title: ANY(${number[]}) does not bind a Postgres array, so team/org auth queries fail
findings.body: Org and team authorization interpolate JavaScript number arrays as Prisma.sql`"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` and `"userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds})` (same pattern at the team-scope user list). Prisma.sql binds each interpolated value as one query parameter; a JS array is not expanded into a PostgreSQL int[]. At execution this typically errors with operator does not exist: integer = text or malformed array literal (the parameter is sent as text/JSON like [1,2,3], not '{1,2,3}'::int[]). Team and org insights then throw instead of returning rows. The length > 0 guard avoids an empty list but does not fix binding. Use a form Prisma actually supports, such as "teamId" IN (${Prisma.join(teamIds)}) or "teamId" = ANY(ARRAY[${Prisma.join(teamIds)}]::int[]), and keep the empty-list guard because Prisma.join([]) produces invalid IN (). The new tests never execute these statements: they deep-compare Sql objects, and the only $queryRaw case is user scope, which has no ANY().

findings.title: Composed-condition assertions compare nested Sql objects to flat templates
findings.body: Team scope (this expect), org scope, and the combined eventTypeId+memberUserId filter expect a single flat Prisma.sql`...` template. The service builds those predicates with reduce, nesting fragments (Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR (${condition})` / AND). Prisma stores nested Sql instances on .values and only flattens them when the query runs, so Vitest toEqual compares different .strings/.values and these tests fail even if the rendered SQL matches. The author noted the suite was not run. User-scope and single-filter expects happen to be one template on both sides and can pass while the composed authorization paths stay red and unexecuted. Assert rendered SQL (or execute team/org conditions with $queryRaw, including a row that must be excluded) instead of structural equality of differently built Sql objects.
